exposure: Pseudoephedrine (PSE) at doses of 25 mg/kg, 50 mg/kg, 100 mg/kg, and 200 mg/kg
cohort: Pregnant rats were divided into a control group and four experimental groups, receiving different doses of pseudoephedrine.
finding: Increasing doses of pseudoephedrine during pregnancy led to decreased morphometric data, ossification rate, bone length, and calcium amount in the bone tissue of rat fetuses.
cross-section timing: On the 21st day of pregnancy (fetal stage)
birth_weight: N/A (fetal weights were measured prior to birth)
gest_age: N/A (study focused on fetal development between day 1 and 20 of pregnancy, with measurements on day 21)
